item.title: A Home for Those Who Served: UF’s Collegiate Veterans Success Center Supports Student Veterans Year-Round
item.description: The University of Florida’s Collegiate Veterans Success Center provides support and community to veterans and military-connected students year-round, not just during Veterans Day week. Located in Yon Hall, the center serves as a resource hub for students who have served in the armed forces or who come from military families. item.title: Preventing the Next Crimea: Behavioral Analysis for Strategic Diplomacy in the Putin Era
item.description: A turning point in U.S.–Russia relations unfolded at the 2007 Munich Security Conference, President Vladimir Putin did more than offer criticism—he firmly rejected the post–Cold War U.S.–led order as illegitimate. Western officials brushed off his remarks as rhetorical posturing. Yet it is now 2025, and that speech unmistakably foreshadowed the trajectory Russia would take: the invasions of Georgia, Crimea, and Ukraine. item.title: Behind Closed Doors: Life Under the Kafala System
item.description: Many immigrant children living in Kuwait learn the meaning of injustice firsthand, often before learning their ABCs. The kafala system, prevalent in the Middle East, allows employers to legally tie workers to them and limits the freedom and rights of foreign workers and their families in many ways. item.title: Alachua County Animal Shelter Planned on UF Land: What It Means for Students
item.description: University of Florida students may soon find a new practical learning space just steps from campus after Alachua County commissioners approved plans to build a new animal shelter on UF-owned property. The new facility, planned near UF’s College of Veterinary Medicine, is intended to replace the county’s decades-old shelter, Alachua County Animal Resources, which struggles with overcrowding and limited resources. item.description: On January 24th, armed federal agents piled on top of a 37-year-old man, shot him, and killed him.
